# pbs_traffic_control_rules (Data Source)

Lists the traffic control rules of a Proxmox Backup Server, with the rates their connections reach now, which change from one read to the next. Needs `Sys.Audit on /`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_traffic_control_rules" "all" {}

# The rates in bytes per second the connections of each rule reach right now:
# they change from one read to the next.
output "traffic_now" {
  value = {
    for r in data.pbs_traffic_control_rules.all.rules :
    r.name => { in = r.current_rate_in, out = r.current_rate_out }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `rules` (Attributes List) The rules, sorted by name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `burst_in` (String) How many bytes over `rate_in` PBS may receive at once, as PBS writes it, such as `10 MiB`; null when not set.
- `burst_out` (String) How many bytes over `rate_out` PBS may send at once, as PBS writes it, such as `10 MiB`; null when not set.
- `comment` (String) Comment; null when there is none.
- `current_rate_in` (Number) Rate at which PBS receives from the rule's connections now, in bytes per second; always `0` without `rate_in`, and for a rule PBS has not applied yet.
- `current_rate_out` (Number) Rate at which PBS sends to the rule's connections now, in bytes per second; always `0` without `rate_out`, and for a rule PBS has not applied yet.
- `name` (String) Rule name, such as `office`.
- `network` (Set of String) Client networks the rule applies to, in CIDR notation.
- `rate_in` (String) Rate limit on the data PBS receives from the matching clients, in bytes per second, as PBS writes it, such as `10 MiB`; null when not set.
- `rate_out` (String) Rate limit on the data PBS sends to the matching clients, in bytes per second, as PBS writes it, such as `10 MiB`; null when not set.
- `timeframe` (Set of String) Times the rule applies at; null for always.
- `users` (Set of String) Users the rule applies to; null for every client.
